back: A material whose properties change in a controlled, usually reversible way in response to a stimulus such as heat, light, pressure, moisture or electricity.
A material developed through new or improved processes to have properties traditional materials cannot offer, e.g. carbon fibre.

front: Modern vs smart — the key difference
back: A modern material is impressive for the properties it has; a smart material is useful because its properties change.
Change colour in ultraviolet light and reverse in the dark — transition lenses, UV security inks, UV indicator wristbands.
Change colour with temperature — baby spoons and bottles, kettles and mugs, battery test strips, chilled food packaging.
A metal alloy that returns to a pre-set shape when heated after being deformed while cool.
An alloy of nickel and titanium — the most widely used SMA.
Spectacle frames that spring back, dental braces, medical stents and thermal safety devices that shut a valve at a set temperature.
Thermoplastic granules that soften at around 62°C in hot water, are shaped by hand, set rigid and tough, and can be reshaped repeatedly.
Enclosing tiny droplets or particles in a protective coating that releases them when broken by pressure, friction or heat.
Micro-capsules in clothing or bedding that absorb heat as they melt and release it as they solidify, evening out temperature.
Technology that identifies a person from a unique biological characteristic — fingerprint, face, iris or voice.
Biometric data cannot be changed if it is stolen, so storage, access and fairness for all users must be considered.
Fibres woven into fabric that carry electrical signals — heated jackets, wearable health monitors, touch-sensitive garments.
Allow a fabric to tighten, loosen or change texture in response to heat or moisture.
